proof_summary: Rewrite each summand as \(\binom Nj N^{\overline j}\): shifting \(N\) by \(k\) leaves the rising factorial unchanged modulo \(k\), while Vandermonde’s identity reduces the binomial change to terms divisible by \(k\), using \(\binom{k}{i}i=k\binom{k-1}{i-1}\) and \(i\mid N^{\overline i}\). Extending the shorter sum by zero binomial terms then allows these termwise congruences to be summed.
